pages.title: Complex Analysis
pages.text: $(thing)Complex Analysis$()$(br2)Add the square root of minus one and every polynomial has its roots. Fourier series and fractals follow.

$(thing)Insight$(): 30$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Calculus.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Real Continuum.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A complex number has modulus r and argument θ, and you want every complex w with wⁿ equal to it. Write the k-th such root in polar form, remembering that the argument is only defined up to whole turns of 2π.
